concepts.name: Useful Simplicity
concepts.description: The principle that information should be simplified enough to guide decisions and actions, even if it is not perfectly complete or precise.

concepts.name: High-Concept Pitch
concepts.description: A compact description that communicates a complex idea by connecting it to familiar concepts or stories.

problems.name: Accurate but unusable communication
problems.description: Information is technically correct but too abstract, complex, or detailed to help people make decisions.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Schemas can be stretched to create complexity
insights.what_it_says: Complex knowledge can be built by repeatedly adapting and extending simple schemas rather than introducing complexity all at once.
insights.why_it_matters: People learn difficult subjects more effectively when new ideas are built on foundations they already understand.

examples_from_source.what_happened: Students first learn trade through a simple apples-and-oranges scenario, then adapt that schema to more advanced situations.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The schema provides a foundation for increasingly sophisticated understanding.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Build advanced knowledge by modifying simple foundational models.

examples_from_source.what_happened: Students begin with idealized pulley problems and later combine or stretch those schemas to solve more complex situations.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: Complex reasoning emerges from reusable building blocks.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Introduce simple models first, then increase complexity gradually.

decision_rules.rule: Teach complexity through progressive schema expansion.
decision_rules.action: Start with simple models and extend them incrementally.
decision_rules.rationale: People learn faster when complexity builds on existing understanding.

patterns.description: Create complex understanding by extending simple mental models.

application_patterns.when_to_use: When teaching, onboarding, or explaining technical concepts.
steps: Connect each addition to the existing model
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Useful in education, training, consulting, and product onboarding.

when_not_to_use: When the audience already possesses advanced schemas
tradeoffs: Progressive learning improves comprehension but may require more time.
insights.evidence: Schemas help us create complex messages from simple materials.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Accessibility is often more valuable than perfect accuracy
insights.what_it_says: Communication should prioritize usefulness and comprehension over perfect technical accuracy when audiences cannot yet understand the more precise explanation.
insights.why_it_matters: An idea that people can understand and apply is more valuable than a perfectly accurate explanation that they cannot use.

examples_from_source.example_name: Solar system model of the atom
examples_from_source.what_happened: Students are taught that electrons orbit the nucleus like planets orbit the sun even though this model is not fully accurate.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The simplified analogy helps learners build understanding before encountering more advanced explanations.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Use simplified models when they help people make sense of unfamiliar ideas.

examples_from_source.what_happened: The technically accurate explanation of electron probability clouds is less useful to beginners than the simplified planetary analogy.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: Accessibility enables learning that would otherwise be impossible.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Provide only as much complexity as the audience can meaningfully use.

decision_rules.condition: When communicating with beginners or non-experts.
decision_rules.action: Provide the simplest explanation that enables understanding and action.
decision_rules.rationale: An unusable truth provides less value than a useful approximation.

patterns.description: Introduce a simplified model before revealing deeper complexity.

warnings.warning: Prioritizing accuracy to the point of uselessness.
warnings.consequence: Audiences fail to understand or apply the information.
warnings.prevention: Communicate only the complexity that is currently useful.

application_patterns.when_to_use: When teaching, onboarding, or presenting specialized knowledge.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Useful in education, leadership, consulting, and technical communication.

when_not_to_use: When precision is legally, medically, or scientifically critical
tradeoffs: Accessibility improves understanding but may temporarily sacrifice precision.
insights.evidence: Accuracy to the point of uselessness is a symptom of the Curse of Knowledge.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Analogies compress complex ideas into memorable pitches
insights.what_it_says: Analogies allow communicators to express complex ideas quickly by linking them to concepts the audience already understands.
insights.why_it_matters: A strong analogy can communicate meaning, structure, and expectations with very few words.

examples_from_source.what_happened: Movies were pitched using familiar references such as 'Die Hard on a bus' or 'Jaws on a spaceship.'
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The audience immediately understands the concept by combining existing schemas.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Use familiar reference points to explain unfamiliar ideas quickly.

decision_rules.rule: Use analogies to communicate complexity quickly.
decision_rules.condition: When explaining a new or abstract idea.
decision_rules.action: Combine the new idea with familiar concepts.
decision_rules.rationale: Existing schemas dramatically reduce explanation time.

patterns.description: Reduce a complex idea to a combination of familiar concepts.
steps: Combine them into a compact statement
Use the analogy as a communication shortcut

application_patterns.when_to_use: When presenting products, stories, strategies, or new concepts.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Useful in marketing, product development, fundraising, and storytelling.

when_not_to_use: When the analogy introduces misleading assumptions
tradeoffs: Analogies improve comprehension but may omit nuance.
insights.evidence: A great way to avoid useless accuracy, and to dodge the Curse of Knowledge, is to use analogies.

relationships.evidence: If a message can't be used to make predictions or decisions, it is without value.
Analogies derive their power from schemas.
Schemas help us create complex messages from simple materials.
Accuracy to the point of uselessness is a symptom of the Curse of Knowledge.
A great way to avoid useless accuracy, and to dodge the Curse of Knowledge, is to use analogies.
